lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Rebuilt weekly carrier scorecards used by 6 regional managers to renegotiate contracts, cutting late deliveries from 11% to 7% in two quarters.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Mapped patient intake at 4 clinics with front-desk staff and cut the recommended intake form from 5 pages to 2 without losing required fields.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Make sure the LinkedIn URL is clickable and remove the protocol/display clutter if your formatting currently includes it.
items.because: Recruiters should be able to reach your profile quickly.

items.says: Consider adding a portfolio only if it contains substantive product work.
items.because: An empty or superficial portfolio creates no value.

items.says: Confirm that the MBA date reflects completion, since June 2025 has passed.
items.because: An outdated expected-graduation presentation can make the resume appear neglected.

items.says: Add relevant honors, leadership, or a concentration only if they are selective or strongly related to product management.
Clarify whether you personally led the redesign, owned a particular part of it, or worked within a broader team.
items.because: “Redesigned” can overstate ownership unless your exact role is clear.

items.says: Identify whether the reduction was measured against a controlled baseline or before-and-after performance.
items.because: The measurement method affects credibility.

items.says: Add the test result’s statistical significance or decision threshold if available.
items.because: Experimental rigor would make it even more persuasive.

items.says: Clarify your role in experiment design, analysis, and rollout rather than allowing “testing” to imply ownership of all three.
Replace emphasis on writing documents with the product decision or customer/business problem you owned.
items.because: Requirements writing is expected from a product manager.

items.says: Clarify whether the early shipment resulted from your work or was simply a team delivery outcome.
items.because: “Two weeks ahead” is weak unless your contribution to that result is evident.

items.says: Use US spelling for “analyzed” if you are applying primarily in the United States.
items.because: The resume currently mixes US context with British spelling.

items.says: Standardize the monetary figure using a currency symbol and abbreviated magnitude.
items.because: Consistency looks more polished.

items.says: Clarify how the estimate was validated.
items.because: Validation makes the business case more credible.

items.says: Clarify whether you personally resolved tickets, coordinated resolution, or improved the triage process.
items.because: Ownership is ambiguous.

items.says: Consider removing this bullet if you need space.
items.because: This bullet is less strategic than the others.

items.says: Clarify what funding or rollout scope resulted, if you can quantify it.
Consider combining its substance with the first onboarding bullet rather than keeping it separate.
items.because: Combining related material would reduce repetition and preserve space.

items.says: Explain your analytical or process contribution beyond rebuilding the reporting format.
Be careful about directly attributing the full late-delivery improvement to the scorecards unless you can support that link.
items.because: A dashboard or scorecard alone rarely produces an operational outcome.

items.says: Specify the measurement period and baseline if available.
Clarify whether the 30% reduction is relative or absolute.
items.because: Percentage reductions can sound larger or smaller depending on the starting point.

items.says: Spell out “Sales and Operations Planning” on first use unless the target audience will universally recognize S&OP.
items.because: Product recruiters may not all know the acronym.

items.says: Clarify whether you created the consensus-forecast process or facilitated an existing process.
items.because: The current wording combines two different levels of ownership.

items.says: Add the business value of the 1,800 saved hours if you can calculate it reliably, such as capacity, service improvement, or verified cost savings.
items.because: Translating it into an operating result would make the impact easier to understand.

items.says: Clarify your role in tool selection, implementation, or change management.
Update “Present” if the project is no longer active.
items.because: Stale “Present” dates are a common credibility issue.

items.says: Indicate that the leadership role is ongoing only if you still perform it regularly.
Standardize “tonnes” to US usage if targeting US employers.
items.because: Consistent regional language also matters.

items.says: Clarify whether 3,100 students were registered, eligible, reached, or active users.
items.because: “Launched to” does not reveal adoption, and exposure is not the same as usage.

items.says: Consider identifying the timeframe behind the nine-ton figure more precisely.
Avoid implying that reminders alone caused all weekly-active-user growth unless you ran an experiment or have supporting analysis.
items.because: Several factors may have influenced it over a full academic term.

items.says: Clarify whether the interviews uncovered missed pickup windows before or after launch.
Clarify the baseline for the 95% fill rate.
Define what “staff cover shifts” means for an external reader.
items.because: The current terminology depends on insider knowledge and lacks context.

items.says: Differentiate the nature of your work across the first two bullets without merely changing the verb.
items.because: Repetition makes distinct accomplishments feel less differentiated.

items.says: Correct the grammar around “annual saving”.
Standardize the number of clinics using the same number style applied elsewhere.
State whether the $2.4M was projected, validated, or realized.
items.because: Distinguishing modeled impact from realized impact protects credibility.

items.says: Explain the analytical principle used to remove fields, such as duplication, regulatory necessity, or workflow relevance.
Be cautious about claiming no required fields were lost unless the client or compliance team verified that conclusion.
items.because: The quality and safety of the recommendation matter in healthcare.

items.says: Consider combining this with the first practicum bullet, since both culminate in approval of the same pilot.
items.because: Repeating the pilot approval uses space without adding a separate outcome.

items.says: Prioritize harder, demonstrable capabilities and remove broad terms that are already evident from your experience.
Use terminology consistently with the bullets; for example, distinguish experiment design from merely participating in A/B testing.
Add proficiency levels only if they are meaningful and defensible.
Include SQL, data visualization, prototyping, analytics, or project-management tools only if you have actually used them.
Consider specifying advanced Excel capabilities rather than listing Excel generically.
items.because: The current tool list is thin for product roles.

items.says: Use one date format throughout and choose either an en dash or hyphen consistently.
Use one convention for numbers; currently some numbers are spelled out while others use numerals.
Standardize US English if US employers are the target: spelling, units, and currency.
Ensure bullets do not break awkwardly across lines in the final PDF.
Use consistent serial commas, especially in lists of functions or stakeholders.
Keep punctuation consistent across all bullets.
Check that every URL is clickable and that the PDF filename is professional.
Verify that the resume remains legible at normal zoom and fits on one page.
